quotes.text: Use the Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API to accept bank transfer payments.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Use the Payment Intents API to accept bank transfer payments.

You must also populate the [customer parameter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create.md#create_payment_intent-customer) of the PaymentIntent creation request. Bank transfers aren’t available on PaymentIntents without a customer.

Stripe sends this event if funds are applied to a PaymentIntent but the payment remains incomplete. Note that when you first confirm a PaymentIntent and it transitions to `requires_action`, Stripe sends `payment_intent.requires_action` instead, even if existing customer balance funds were applied at the same time.
Bank transfer is also a *delayed notification payment method*

findings: The November 7 capture is only a variant index: new raw lines 5-17 document the article purpose and four navigation links, not prerequisites, field schemas, webhooks, settlement, or payment results. The May 5 capture (old raw lines 1-2180) remains the dated detailed source; the diff's apparent mass deletion (diff lines 3-2187) is a representation change, not evidence that prior requirements or routes were retired.

The new headline explicitly includes Checkout Sessions alongside Payment Intents (new raw line 7 versus old raw line 6). The new Elements/Checkout Sessions variant link (new raw lines 13-15) is a discoverable additional route; the old detailed Elements section was PaymentIntent based (old raw lines 54-85), while the old capture already had a separate hosted Checkout section (old raw lines 940-954). No linked variant was read, so no new Elements Checkout Session flow is established.

The current summary only cites the May 5 raw (current source lines 4-8, 66-68) and presents detailed older claims without dating them in the body (current source lines 11-64). Its scope/route should identify the November index and retain the historical raw, including the new variant links as navigation rather than behavior. Root to provider to concept route was read at wiki/index.md lines 5-7, wiki/stripe-index.md lines 308-313, and wiki/concepts/stripe-bank-transfers.md lines 104-140.

A separate baseline accuracy issue exists: current source lines 21-27 say JP and MX bank-transfer types require return_url unconditionally. Old raw Elements automatic-method examples contain return_url (old raw lines 153-187), but manual PaymentIntent examples for JP and MX omit it (old raw lines 287-341); Direct API automatic-method examples include it for every region (old raw lines 1394-1511), while Direct API manual examples omit it (old raw lines 1623-1685). The source must scope that claim to the illustrated flow rather than assert a region-wide requirement.

Current source line 25 says an EU manual FR country option localizes to the customer's country. Old raw lines 260-285 and 1853-1858 distinguish manual country selection from Dashboard-managed Customer/account-country fallback. The summary conflates those modes.

The old raw treats a first confirmation with insufficient balance as payment_intent.requires_action even when partial pre-existing balance applies, then later insufficient incoming funds as payment_intent.partially_funded (old raw lines 722-742 and 1954-1976). Current source lines 33-41 should keep the status/event distinction and add the consequential amount-change effect: funds return to customer balance and may fund other open PaymentIntents; manual reconciliation needs reapplication (old raw line 742 or 1974).

Checkout form submission and checkout.session.completed are not paid status: old raw lines 1182-1205 distinguish hosted instructions and waiting from checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/PaymentIntent succeeded. Browser return likewise requires status inspection (old raw lines 594-603).
substantive_changes: Explicit headline scope expands from Payment Intents API (old raw line 6) to Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API (new raw line 7). This is an article-scope statement, not a proven change in bank-transfer runtime support.

The new index exposes an Elements Checkout Sessions API variant beside the Elements Payment Intents API variant (new raw lines 13-15). Its behavior and prerequisites are unverified because the target variant content is not in the pinned capture.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 5 Customer-associated PaymentIntent and Checkout Session requirements as dated detail, not November-confirmed behavior (old raw lines 71-89, 950-1000; current source lines 17-19, 50). The Accounts v2 recommendation is preview-qualified for non-Connect users in old raw lines 8-14 and should not be collapsed into an unqualified Customer/Account equivalence.

Preserve underpayment/overpayment and reconciliation distinctions as May 5 claims (old raw lines 28-50), and distinguish PaymentIntent partial funding from invoices remaining open. Changing a partially funded Intent amount returns funds and may automatically fund other Intents (old raw lines 738-742, 1968-1974).

Preserve old Checkout payment-only, one-time, single-currency, Customer-associated and delayed-notification constraints with May 5 provenance (old raw lines 950-975), and distinguish checkout.session.completed from async_payment_succeeded (old raw lines 1182-1205).

Preserve old mode/UI qualifiers: Elements PaymentIntent confirmation and return_url/status inspection (old raw lines 494-603); Direct API server confirmation, client-displayed next_action instructions and live versus test bank details (old raw lines 1384-1413, 1700-1715); optional Dashboard instruction emails with sandbox restriction (old raw lines 711-720, 1207-1216); sandbox-only funding simulations (old raw lines 798-806, 2030-2116).

Preserve older regional and version qualifiers as dated, including IBAN localization branches and Spain limitation (old raw lines 144-151, 260-285, 1853-1858), latest-API automatic_payment_methods optionality (old raw lines 189, 1513), and temporary rate-limit error (old raw lines 930-938, 2118-2126). The index does not renew their current validity.
conflicts: Current source lines 26-27 assert unconditional JP/MX return_url requirements, but old raw manual PaymentIntent examples at lines 287-341 and 1623-1685 omit it; old raw automatic examples at lines 153-187 and 1469-1511 include it. Scope the source and matching concept table at wiki/concepts/stripe-bank-transfers.md lines 108-114 to the actual UI/integration mode.

Current source line 25 and wiki/concepts/stripe-bank-transfers.md line 112 imply manual EU country selection is based on Customer country; old raw lines 260-285 and 1853-1858 distinguish explicit request country from Dashboard-managed fallback.
unresolved_questions: The contents and current requirements of the new Elements Checkout Sessions variant, and current validity of the May 5 detailed variants, remain unresolved because only their November index links were pinned (new raw lines 11-17).

The new index does not settle whether older Accounts v2 preview, regional availability, return_url behavior, or checkout/fulfillment details changed after May 5 (new raw lines 7-17; old raw lines 8-14, 83-85, 940-975, 1182-1205).

findings: Add November index provenance and explicit four-variant route, with the Elements Checkout Sessions link identified as navigation only (new raw lines 7-17); retain older detailed raw and its May 5 capture date (current source lines 4-8, 66-68).
Correct baseline overclaims in the region table and EU localization note (current source lines 21-27 versus old raw lines 153-187, 260-341, 1469-1511, 1623-1685, 1853-1858).
Clarify the partial funding event/status distinction, amount-change side effect, and Checkout submission versus paid outcome (current source lines 33-50; old raw lines 722-744, 1182-1205, 1954-1976).
conflicts: Unconditional JP/MX return_url claim conflicts with manual PaymentIntent examples (current source lines 26-27; old raw lines 287-341, 1623-1685).
EU customer-country localization claim conflates Dashboard-managed and explicitly selected manual country (current source line 25; old raw lines 260-285, 1853-1858).
source_assessments.reason: The new same-URL capture changes explicit article scope and navigation but omits all detailed flow text; the existing May 5 summary also has independently discoverable baseline inaccuracies. A dated source update is needed without replacing the old evidence or asserting new variant behavior.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bank-transfers/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture says bank transfers can be accepted with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents and links four UI/API variants (new raw lines 5-17); it supplies no implementation prerequisites, state transitions, or outcome evidence. The old capture's PaymentIntent and Checkout details require an associated Customer in their respective May 5 flows (old raw lines 71-85 and 950-1000), distinguish a Customer cash balance, PaymentIntent, Checkout Session and invoice, and keep insufficient/partial funding apart from succeeded payment (old raw lines 28-50, 722-744, 1182-1205). The mapped source-stripe-bank-transfers-accept-payment.md summarizes that older guide at lines 11-64 but needs new index routing and correction of its unqualified JP/MX return_url and EU localization table claims at lines 21-27.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bank-transfers/accept-a-payment, the substantive documented change is the broader Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents headline (new raw line 7 versus old raw line 6); the four links, including an Elements Checkout Sessions API route, are navigation and do not establish the linked variant's flow (new raw lines 11-17). The mass diff removal is a format/index shift, so source-stripe-bank-transfers-accept-payment.md must preserve May 5 claims with their date: Customer prerequisites, manual versus Dashboard EU country, conditional return_url examples, webhook funding states, and delayed Checkout fulfillment (old raw lines 71-85, 260-341, 722-744, 950-975, 1182-1205, 1853-1858; current source lines 17-50). Its JP/MX and EU table wording needs reciprocal correction in the bank-transfer concept. Client return or Checkout submission proves no funds; paid status requires the appropriate succeeded event/status, while test helpers and live bank details have distinct environments (old raw lines 594-603, 1202-1205, 1700-1705).
